hints: Changing a length x to a target T costs |x-T|.
The sum of absolute distances is minimized at a median, not necessarily the mean.
Sort and choose the middle value; for even n, any value between the two middle values is optimal.
analogy: Place a shared meeting point so the total walking distance is smallest; a median balances people on each side.
algorithm: Sort the lengths, take the middle element as target, and sum absolute differences.
correctness: If the target moves away from a median, at least as many values become farther as become closer; thus a median minimizes total absolute change.
complexity: O(n log n) time and O(1) extra space beyond sorting.
